two_witness.note: the letter-corrupted tokens are exactly the cells where the OCR lost the minus; for those the sign comes from the ink only

case1.solution: u(y) = G/(2 mu) y (H-y), U_max = G H^2/(8 mu)

parabola_reproduced_exactly.note: 2nd-order central differences integrate a quadratic exactly -> zero discretisation error for Poiseuille

convergence.manufactured_solution: u = sin(pi y), -mu u'' = mu pi^2 sin(pi y)

case3.solution: u=U cos(kx) sin(ky) e^{-2 nu k^2 t}, v=-U sin(kx) cos(ky) e^{-2 nu k^2 t}, p=-U^2/4 (cos2kx+cos2ky) e^{-4 nu k^2 t}

case4.note: Re->0 limit of the lid-driven cavity is the biharmonic Stokes problem grad^4 psi = 0, psi = psi_n = 0 on the walls, psi_n = -U on the lid; the separable corner family spans its exact solution space

stokes.note: p is reconstructed by path integration of mu*lap(u); both momentum components are then re-verified by differentiating p

reference_grid.interpretation: Ghia's tables come from the 129x129 line (differential) solver; a 257x257 grid is also shown for Re=400 in the same paper

evidence.re_definition: Re = U_lid * L / nu with L = cavity side, U_lid = lid speed
evidence.normalisation: u and v divided by U_lid; lengths by L
evidence.profile_definitions: Table I: x/L = 0.5 vertical line, u(y); Table II: y/L = 0.5 horizontal line, v(x)
evidence.origin_and_lid: origin at the lower-left corner, lid at y/L = 1 moving in +x
evidence.lattice_consumption_caveat: for a D3Q19-BGK consumer: Re = U*N_eff/nu with nu = (tau-1/2)/3; half-way bounce-back places the wall half a lattice cell outside the boundary node, so N_eff = N-1. Using N instead of N-1 biases Re by 1/N (1.2% at N=81, 0.8% at N=129), which is the same order as the 3% acceptance band and must be stated with any comparison.

criteria.statement: internal consistency of the registered tables

figures.caption: Registered Ghia (1982) Table I/II profiles for Re=100/400/1000 (digits from the PDF text layer, signs from the page raster).
Ink-width sign witness: every value column splits into two cleanly separated clusters (unsigned ~27 pt, signed ~31.5 pt).
Incompressibility invariants on the registered tables (∫u dy = 0 along x/L=0.5, ∫v dx = 0 along y/L=0.5).
Poiseuille/Couette analytic anchors and the measured second-order convergence slope of the channel discretisation.
Taylor-Green vortex: analytic vorticity field and energy decay; spectral residual of the NS operator is at roundoff.
Cavity creeping-limit solution space: the separable biharmonic corner mode (λ = 2.7396) that spans the Stokes-limit field.

environment.pymupdf: PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3: Python bindings for the MuPDF 1.27.2 library.

in_repo_secondary_table_defect.boundary_condition_violation: the in-repo table gives u(y=1)=0.0 although the lid moves with u=1.0, and it has no point at y=0; both are visible in the per-profile comparison above
in_repo_secondary_table_defect.recommendation: consumers should read the anchor registered here (papers/artifacts/w26/d3q19-bgk-analytic-fourcase/anchor_register.json) instead of the in-repo transcription; the in-repo file is left untouched because other code imports it

limits: The digits come from the OCR text layer of a scan; the OCR was verified only through structural checks (1/128 lattice, right alignment, conservation invariants), not against a second independent typesetting of the paper.
The four analytic cases are operator/consistency anchors, not a solver-accuracy claim: no lattice-Boltzmann simulation is compared with the Ghia tables here.
Case 4 (creeping limit) is checked on the separable biharmonic family and the Stokes pressure integrability; the corner eigenvalue enters only as a parameter.
